site.name: Tsukimi-tei 月見亭
site.concept: A seven-seat kappō counter in Yanaka serving seasonal kaiseki rooted in Edo-period Tokyo cookery, with sake from sixteen prefectures.

card_pattern: Cards sit on the kraft surface with no border — only a thin sumi hairline at the top, generous interior padding (2.4rem), and a small kamon (umebachi or tsuru) anchored to the upper-right corner at 18px. Title in Shippori Mincho 500, supporting copy in Inter 300 with line-height 1.8. One-line price or season label sits at the bottom in indigo, separated by 3rem of empty space — the void is part of the unit.
design_rules: Compose every page asymmetrically: weight pulled to the left third or right third, balanced by deliberate emptiness occupying at least 30% of the viewport. Wagara patterns appear only as 6–10% opacity backgrounds; kamon appear once per section as formal seals, never repeated as wallpaper. Vertical rhythm dominates — long narrow text columns, generous 1.8 line-height, single cinnabar accent reserved for marks of season or emphasis.

pages.title: 月見亭 Tsukimi-tei — Kappō Counter, Yanaka
pages.content_brief: Hero with vertical-set Japanese title 月見亭 paired with romaji subtitle, off-center to the left, balanced by a single tsuru-no-maru seal in the right negative space. Brief manifesto: 'Seven seats. One counter. The season decided this morning at Toyosu.' Tonight's date and current course price (¥18,000, eight courses) shown beneath. Single cinnabar dot marks the current season — late autumn, 2024.

pages.title: Course — Tsukimi-tei
pages.content_brief: The omakase progression for the current fortnight (Oct 28 – Nov 10). Eight courses listed vertically with Japanese name, Latin transliteration, and one-line ingredient note: Sakizuke (kaki shiratama, persimmon and tofu), Wanmono (matsutake dobin-mushi), Mukōzuke (akami zuke from Misaki), Yakimono (charcoal-grilled sawara, hōba leaf), Takiawase (kabocha and shungiku), Shiizakana (duck tsumire), Gohan (shinmai with ikura), Mizumono (kuromitsu warabi-mochi). No photographs.

pages.title: Sake — Sixteen Prefectures
pages.content_brief: Sake list organized by region, north to south. Each entry: brewery name in kanji and romaji, prefecture, rice varietal, seimaibuai polish percentage, and pour price (90ml / 180ml). Highlights: Hiroki Junmai Daiginjō (Fukushima, Yamada-Nishiki 40%), Kokuryū Ishidaya (Fukui), Jūyondai Honmaru (Yamagata). Short note on the chef's preference for warmed junmai with the wanmono course.

pages.title: The Counter — Tsukimi-tei
pages.content_brief: Profile of chef Iwasaki Sōta, who trained eleven years at Kyōtō Kitcho before opening Tsukimi-tei in March 2019 in a 1923 machiya off Yanaka Ginza. Cypress counter milled from a single Yoshino log. Philosophy paragraph on shun (peak-season) and the deliberate restraint inherited from Edo-period shōjin tradition. Closing line set vertically: '一期一会' with translation.

pages.title: Reservations — Tsukimi-tei
pages.content_brief: Two seatings nightly: 17:30 and 20:30. Reserve by telephone only — 03-3823-XXXX, between 14:00 and 16:00. Two-week deposit policy (¥10,000 per seat, refundable up to 72 hours prior). Closed Sundays and the second Tuesday of each month. Children under twelve not seated. Form is a single block of instructions, not fields — emphasizes the analog booking culture.

pages.title: Visit — Yanaka, Taitō-ku
pages.content_brief: Address: 3-14-7 Yanaka, Taitō-ku, Tōkyō 110-0001. Six minutes on foot from Nippori station (JR Yamanote, west exit), past Yūyake Dandan. Look for the indigo noren under a single paulownia. No signage in English. Hours block, transit notes, and a short courtesy paragraph requesting guests arrive within ten minutes of seating to preserve the course timing for the counter.
